OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: "(?s).*\\S.*"
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: "(?s).*\\S.*"
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped;
            a leading '+' and country code are kept, otherwise country code '+61'
            is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the national
            digits. The result must be a '+' followed by 8 to 15 digits; this
            E.164 value is stored and returned. For example '0412 345 678' is
            stored as '+61412345678'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when supplied it must
            be a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned
            lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' form.
            Optional on create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current
            date. The stored value is returned on read.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true, allows creating this owner even if another owner already
            has the same last name and address (same household). Write-only flag
            used only on create; it is never stored or returned.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: true
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone

## Summary

I added address normalization to owner creation in `OwnerRestControllerV1.java`, following the same pattern already used for telephone and email normalization.

**Changes in `src/main/java/.../rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`:**

1. **New `normalizeAddress` method** that:
   - Trims and collapses internal whitespace runs to a single space
   - Upper-cases the value
   - Expands common street-type abbreviations per token via a lookup map (`ST→STREET`, `RD→ROAD`, `AVE→AVENUE`)
   - Throws `400 BAD_REQUEST` if the address is **blank after normalization** (the required-field check)

2. **Applied it in `addOwner`** right after email normalization:
   ```java
   owner.setAddress(normalizeAddress(owner.getAddress()));
   ```
   This happens *before* the household-duplicate check and `assignHousehold`, so both the duplicate detection (`isHouseholdInUse`) and the shared household id (`householdIdFor`) now operate on the normalized `owner.getAddress()`. The normalized value is also what gets stored and returned.

Since every newly created owner is stored with its normalized address, all subsequent household comparisons in `ClinicServiceImpl` (which additionally lower-case/collapse via `normalizeForHousehold`) compare normalized forms consistently.

**Verification against the tests:**
- `"  12  main  st "` → `"12 MAIN STREET"` ✓
- `"7 elm ave"` → `"7 ELM AVENUE"` ✓
- `"   "` → blank after normalization → `400` ✓

I scoped the change to creation only (`addOwner`), per the spec's "whenever an owner is created"; `updateOwner` was left untouched.
